claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9110 §4.2.1: "If the port subcomponent is empty or not given, TCP port 80 (the reserved port for WWW services) is the default." §4.2.2: "... TCP port 443 (the reserved port for HTTP over TLS) is the default."

Name-resolution half: RFC 9110 §4.3.2 registered name "is an indirect identifier for use with a name resolution service, such as DNS, to find an address"; client resolves "the host identifier to an IP address, establishing a TCP connection to that address". Localhost half: in the lab (r3) `getent ahosts localhost` returns "::1" first, then "127.0.0.1"; /etc/hosts lists both. So localhost is not only 127.0.0.1. RFC 6761 not in refs/ nor a versions.yaml root.

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9110 §4.3.2: "establishing a TCP connection to that address on the indicated port". Compose @stage-0: lab ports "8080:8080", "8443:8443"; web `network_mode: "service:lab"` (Caddy shares the lab's network). Run r3: step 2 "connected to port 8080", step 4 "HTTP/1.1 200 OK".

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9112 §9.7: "It initiates a connection to the server on the appropriate port and sends the TLS ClientHello to begin the TLS handshake. When the TLS handshake has finished, the client may then initiate the first HTTP request."

RFC 9110 §7.1: "the client sends a request message containing enough components of its parsed target URI to enable recipients to identify that same resource." One target per request. The network-tab half rests on claim 21 (unverified).

RFC 9112 §4: "The first line of a response message is the status-line, consisting of the protocol version, a space (SP), the status code, and another space and ending with an OPTIONAL textual phrase". Run r3: first line "HTTP/1.1 200 OK". r2: /slow gave "HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable".

Fetching of img/link/script on its own vs following a hyperlink only on activation, and scripts sending later requests, are HTML Living Standard behaviour; no docs root in content/versions.yaml and no refs/ copy. Not fetched. www/index.html only shows the markup.

RFC 9112 §9.7: first request only "When the TLS handshake has finished".

issues.quote: Your address carries three things: a scheme (`http` or `https`, before `://`), a host name and a port.
issues.text: The address also carries a path (RFC 9110 §4.2.1: authority path-abempty; claim 16 includes it), and the port is optional (next clause says so). The lab's own address `http://localhost:8080/index.html` carries `/index.html`; two paragraphs later the lesson calls the path "the part of the address after the host and port", contradicting "three things".
issues.fix: Write: "Your address carries a scheme (`http` or `https`, before `://`), a host name, an optional port and a path." Keep the path definition in the next paragraph unchanged.

issues.quote: `localhost` is a name that always means the machine you are on, address `127.0.0.1`.
issues.text: localhost also resolves to the IPv6 loopback ::1; in the lab `getent ahosts localhost` returns ::1 first, then 127.0.0.1. "address 127.0.0.1" states one address as the only one (claim 2, rephrased).
issues.fix: Write "... the machine you are on, usually address `127.0.0.1`"; update claim 2 to match.

issues.quote: a local list of name-to-address lines your machine usually checks before asking DNS
issues.text: Claims 7, 14, 21 and the hosts-file-before-DNS part of claim 10 rest on sources outside content/versions.yaml (HTML Living Standard, browser devtools, host OS resolver) and stay unverified. Behaviour claims, hedged in the text; not blocking.
issues.fix: Owner decision (open_questions): add a browser/HTML docs root to versions.yaml, or keep the hedged wording as is.

issues.quote: Only the HTTPS port runs encryption, hence `donhang.local:8443` instead of `localhost:8080`.
issues.text: Section 2 showed my browser failing on donhang.local, yet here the script uses that name with no comment. I only learn why it works inside the lab at the very end of section 6 ("The lab lists `donhang.local` in its own hosts file."), so in section 5 I stop and wonder whether step 3 will fail too.
issues.fix: Add half a sentence to the step 3 bullet: "the lab lists `donhang.local` in its own hosts file, so the name works for the script".

issues.quote: Step 4: `-D -` prints what came back instead of the page, and `-o /dev/null` throws the page away.
issues.text: "what came back instead of the page" confuses me: the page also came back. I can only work out that it means the lines sent before the page after reading the "..." note under the output.
issues.fix: Write "`-D -` prints the lines the server sends before the page" and keep the rest of the sentence.

issues.quote: B->>S: ask again for each file the page embeds
issues.text: Every earlier ask has a return arrow, but the last one has none, and the "draw" step the prose and the chain definition name is not in the diagram. I can narrate it, but I end the diagram unsure whether those files come back before drawing.
issues.fix: Say in the paragraph after the diagram that each embedded file comes back in its own response, as the earlier arrows show, and that drawing is not shown.

issues.quote: You start the lab — the programs `scripts/up.sh` runs on your machine, with names and addresses of its own, so it behaves like a separate machine — and open `http://localhost:8080/index.html` in your browser;
issues.text: The opening sentence holds two inserted definitions (lab, localhost) around the main action; I read it twice to find what I actually do. Later "the machine, the connection, or Caddy" leaves me unsure which machine is meant: mine or the lab.
issues.fix: Split into two sentences: first what the lab is, then "Open `http://localhost:8080/index.html` …"; write "your machine" in the colleague sentence if that is meant.
